title: The Small Quasi-Kernel Conjecture
statement:
Let $D$ be a sourceless digraph on $n$ vertices. A **quasi-kernel** is an independent set $Q$ such that every vertex $u$ of $D$ has a vertex $v\in Q$ with $\operatorname{dist}(v,u)\leq 2$.

**Small Quasi-Kernel Conjecture.** The digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel of order at most $\frac{n}{2}$.

Sources without vertices have no immediate obstruction from isolated source vertices to a small quasi-kernel, motivating this conjecture of Erdős and Székely from 1976. The conjecture was initially communicated orally and later appeared in print; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Alexander Clow, “Greedily Constructing Small Quasi-Kernels”, arXiv:2601.11847 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.11847

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).
